title: Recover an incident and write a handover
goal: Combine service configuration, access and startup evidence into a recoverable repair.
challenge: Recover ll-incident.service without world-readable configuration or a root worker. Its configuration is missing and startup is disabled. An original data file is retained in /usr/local/share/learning-lab/admin-originals/incident.conf. Preserve evidence, restore correct access, verify behavior and startup policy, then write a short handover with rollback steps.

steps.command: work=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/admin-incident.XXXXXX") && cd "$work" && pwd; systemctl status ll-incident.service --no-pager; systemctl is-enabled ll-incident.service
steps.explanation: Use a fresh private evidence directory. Stop if setup fails. Gather current symptoms before a repair.
steps.expected: Inactive/disabled; evidence directory is inside the guest home.

steps.command: sudo systemctl start ll-incident.service; sudo journalctl -u ll-incident.service -n 10 --no-pager; ls -l /etc/learning-lab/incident.conf
steps.explanation: Correlate the failure with the absent file, rather than running the worker as root.

steps.command: sudo install -o root -g ll-service -m 0640 /usr/local/share/learning-lab/admin-originals/incident.conf /etc/learning-lab/incident.conf; sudo runuser -u ll-service -- cat /etc/learning-lab/incident.conf
steps.explanation: Install an exact retained data file with explicit ownership and access. Equivalent supported guest commands are valid if they preserve content and least privilege.
steps.expected: root:ll-service 0640 and a permitted service-account read.

steps.command: sudo systemctl enable --now ll-incident.service; sleep 1; systemctl is-enabled ll-incident.service; sudo journalctl -u ll-incident.service -n 8 --no-pager
steps.explanation: Establish startup policy and a new successful invocation. Enable output alone does not prove future boot success; retain that limitation.
steps.expected: enabled and a fresh LAB_READY from the unprivileged worker.

steps.explanation: Write symptoms, causal evidence, exact changes, verification, remaining uncertainty and rollback. Include the original missing-file/disabled state; no placeholder report counts as completed work.
steps.expected: Your own short report; no app score or automatic inspection.

steps.command: cat handover.txt; sudo systemctl disable --now ll-incident.service
steps.explanation: Review the report and leave the worker stopped/dormant. Keep the repaired config and evidence.
steps.expected: A supported conclusion; no live lab worker remains.

hints: A missing file and disabled startup are distinct facts. Repair and verify each.
Use explicit owner/group/mode when restoring the retained configuration.
Describe what was observed, what was changed and what a future boot still needs to verify.
review: My report records actual symptoms, minimal repair and verification.
The service stayed unprivileged, access stayed narrow, and I left it stopped.
I documented rollback and the limit of enabled-state evidence.
coverage: Partial LPIC-2 202.1 and LPIC-1 104.5/108.2 reinforcement. Guest-only administration; completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
